system_description.narrative_title: U.S.-Iran war, Hormuz blockade and global oil-market disruption
system_description.narrative_summary: A military-diplomatic confrontation between the United States and Iran — amplified by Houthi attacks and regional alignments — is driving efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, imposing sanctions and flight/shipping disruptions, and producing volatile oil markets. As an open system, the conflict links flows (oil, goods, information), regulatory levers (sanctions, flight bans), and force projection (naval escorts, strikes, allied deployments) through reinforcing and balancing feedbacks: military actions provoke market and logistical reactions, which in turn shape diplomatic offers and domestic political constraints. The result is tightly coupled volatility across regional security, global energy supply chains, and financial markets.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: U.S.-Iran military exchanges and negotiations, Houthi attacks, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping routes, oil export volumes and rerouting (pipelines, ship-to-ship transfers), sanctions and air/sea flight suspensions, regional state responses and allied military deployments, and resulting oil-price and market volatility.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and trading infrastructure
Regional Middle East security and alliance networks
International sanctions and aviation/transport regulatory systems
evidence_headlines: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz within 7 days and restart nuclear talks

Allies unite behind Saudi Arabia as Houthis step up attacks

variables.name: Military-diplomatic exchange intensity
variables.description: Measures the overall intensity of hostile military actions, coercive operations, and adversarial diplomatic posturing between opposing actors in the region.

variables.name: Maritime access restriction level
variables.description: Measures the degree to which key sea lanes and chokepoints are restricted, closed, or contested for commercial navigation.

variables.name: Shipping disruption rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and magnitude of interruptions to commercial shipping (attacks, seizures, route closures, or delays) per unit time.

variables.name: Regional oil export throughput
variables.description: Measures the volumetric flow of crude oil and fuel exports leaving the region per unit time through maritime and pipeline channels.

variables.name: Alternative routing capacity
variables.description: Measures the available spare capacity of alternative export channels (pipelines, ship‑to‑ship transfers, alternate ports) to absorb displaced flows.

variables.name: Sanctions scope and severity
variables.description: Measures the breadth and strictness of economic, trade, and transport restrictions applied to parties and commodities related to the conflict.

variables.name: Aviation traffic restriction level
variables.description: Measures the extent of flight bans, airspace closures, and airline suspensions affecting commercial air routes in and through the region.

variables.name: Naval escort and deployment scale
variables.description: Measures the scale and intensity of deployed maritime security assets and escort operations protecting commercial shipping.

variables.name: Attack incident rate on maritime assets
variables.description: Measures the rate at which hostile incidents (missile strikes, drone attacks, sabotage, piracy) occur against vessels and offshore facilities.

variables.name: Oil market price volatility
variables.description: Measures short‑term variability and uncertainty in crude oil and refined product prices in global markets.

variables.name: Derivatives market liquidity
variables.description: Measures the depth and ease of trading in oil futures, options, and other derivatives instruments (bid-ask spreads, open interest, trading volume).

variables.name: War-risk insurance premium level
variables.description: Measures the cost of war-risk and piracy insurance for shipping and offshore assets across affected routes.

variables.name: Diplomatic negotiation intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, scale, and seriousness of mediated talks, ceasefire proposals, and negotiated de‑escalation efforts.

variables.name: Regional coalition cohesion
variables.description: Measures the degree of alignment, coordination, and unified action among regional actors influencing security and economic responses.

variables.name: Logistics delay backlog
variables.description: Measures the accumulated delay and backlog in maritime and overland supply chains affecting delivery times and inventories.

variables.name: Market risk-premium sentiment
variables.description: Measures investor and market participant perception of geopolitical risk expressed as additional risk premia demanded across energy and financial markets.

catalysts.title: US decision on Iran's 7-day Hormuz ceasefire offer
catalysts.description: A near-term US acceptance or rejection of Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, determining immediate de‑escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Driven by: "Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz within 7 days..." and reports of US rejection of the proposal

catalysts.title: Ongoing US–Iran phased deal negotiations
catalysts.description: Continued talks (including U.N. discussions) on a phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end the blockade, potentially incremental and protracted.
catalysts.rationale: Grounded in: "US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz" and U.N. talks coverage

catalysts.title: Surge of Houthi attacks on facilities and shipping
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities, ports and possibly shipping lanes, prompting allied security responses and supply disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: "Houthis say they attacked Riyadh and Aramco facilities" and "Houthis step up attacks; allies unite behind Saudi"

catalysts.title: Allied naval deployments and escorted convoys expand
catalysts.description: France and other partners deploying forces to protect Red Sea and Gulf routes, increasing escort operations and maritime presence.
catalysts.rationale: Cited by: "France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route" and related deployment headlines

catalysts.title: Ship‑to‑ship transfer capacity reaches limits
catalysts.description: Gulf of Oman ship‑to‑ship transfers have hit practical limits as Saudi exports surge, constraining rerouting and increasing delays.
catalysts.rationale: From: "Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge" and DP World rerouting coverage

catalysts.title: Resumption of Saudi East‑West pipeline loadings
catalysts.description: Restarting loadings on the East‑West pipeline would divert crude away from Hormuz, easing maritime pressure and rerouting flows.
catalysts.rationale: Based on: "Saudi East-West Pipeline building up volumes, loading yet to resume" and high Saudi export levels

catalysts.title: Expanded US sanctions on Iranian transport and flights
catalysts.description: Further U.S. measures targeting Iranian aviation and transport networks (continuing recent flight shutdowns) restrict logistics and connectivity.
catalysts.rationale: Prompted by: "New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights" and "UAE halts Iranian flights over US sanctions"

catalysts.title: Rapid oil‑market repricing after diplomatic or attack news
catalysts.description: Options, futures and physical markets react quickly to truce signals or new attacks, driving short‑term volatility and liquidity shifts.
catalysts.rationale: Supported by: "Oil prices fall as U.S.-Iran diplomacy..." and "The options market is sending a contrarian signal" plus Houthi attack price moves
